text:
Zoe: Quick notewe've got a steady uptick in tool_call.output schema rejects on the latest canary variant. Small but consistent.
Priya: Where is it hitting? console or dedicated?
Zoe: Mostly /invoke/tool and /chat/stream. Console shows ~3.7% rejects over 45m.
Miguel: Any sample lines?
Zoe: ```
ValidationError: tool_call.output - wrong type for 'results'
payload: {"tool":"email","output":"Sent ticket #567"}
expected schema: {"tool": "string", "results": [{"id":"string","status":"string"}]}
```
Dan: So model returned a freeform string instead of structured array. Could be prompt tweak or a new model decoder change.
Priya: Is our current behavior to route these to the degen path or to reject and fallback? I forget the config for canaries.
Miguel: Canary routing currently: strict validate -> if pass serve; if reject -> route to permissive model variant (degen) and mark as 'schema-fallback'. Billing: rejects are non-billable, degen responses billable.
Zoe: That's the problemops is seeing rejects as "failed" and paging on strictness meters even though users still get responses via degen.
Dan: Can we split metrics in console: strict_rejects (non-billable) vs degen_served (billable)? Right now the strict_rejects metric rolls up to the same alert.
Priya: Also UX ask: when degen serves, show a small inline tag "served with relaxed schema" and link to sample payloads. Support needs that context.
Miguel: Telemetry idea: deterministic sample rejects using hash(customer_id + route) at 2% but increase to 25% for canary customers. That gives us representative payloads without exploding storage.
ops-bot: Telemetry rule update queued: 'det-sample-toolcall-rejects' (2% global, 25% canary)
Dan: On gating: we should propose an auto-pause rule: if strict_reject_rate > 5% AND degen_served rate < 80% of traffic for 10m -> auto-pause canary + notify owners. Rationale: a lot of rejects with no fallback success means user impact.
Priya: I like that but replace the 80% with "fallback success rate" i.e. fraction of rejected requests that successfully returned usable degen output.
Miguel: Also we need to decide billing mapping. Right now some internal customers get confused because rejects increment the "strictness" meter which triggers quota throttles. We should make strict_rejects not influence quota consumption at all. Quotas should use final_served_status.
Zoe: Yup. Quota mapping change would be: charge on final path (served_strict | served_degen | failed). If degen served, bill normally; if failed, no bill. That avoids double-counting.
Dan: API housekeeping: add optional response meta field: "validation_hint": "soft-invalid" | "hard-reject" | "ok" so downstream adapters can route correctly without guessing. Small change but helps tooling.
Priya: Will that be part of the canary SDK contract change? Need to coordinate with mobile/web SDKs.
Miguel: It's backward-compatible (optional field). We'll add to the contract docs and mark for SDK flag in the next minor.
ops-bot: New console ticket created: DASH-ENGPLAT - "toolcall: split strict_reject vs degen_served + sample panel" (owner: Priya).
deploy-bot: Sampling rule deployed to telemetry-prod: det-sample-toolcall-rejects (2% global, 25% canary).
Zoe: Action list: Priya - dashboard + UX tag; Miguel - implement deterministic sampler and final_served_status billing mapping proposal; Dan - write auto-pause gating RFC; I'll collect 500 reject samples and paste in thread.
Priya: I'll also add a tooltip explaining "validation_hint" values and update support runbook.
Miguel: One more consideration: do we treat structured soft-invalids as eligible for core-model metrics? We should exclude them from strict model perf dashboards to avoid skew.
Dan: Agreedadd a filter in perf dashboards: only include served_strict results.
Zoe: If the spike persists after the sampling window, we may rollback the canary. For now let's gather data.
Priya: Noted.
Zoe: Thanks all, will post samples in 20m. :eyes:
